subject: When to put ~~c(0)* between two factor variables?

messages.author: e5c4db1a1cffab6b
messages.subject: When to put ~~c(0)* between two factor variables?
parts:
In this example, what is the meaning of having that the covariance is 0? Namely: ind60 ~~c(0)* dem60

When should this be used ~~c(0)* ?

myModel <- ' # latent variables
ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3 
dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 
dem65 =~ y5 + y6 + y7 + y8 
# regressions 
dem60 ~ ind60 
dem65 ~ ind60 + dem60 
#   covariances 
  ind60 ~~c(0)* dem60 
'

Many thanks
Ale Dea

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: When to put ~~c(0)* between two factor variables?
parts:
it means that you are forcing the covariance/correlation between factor to be equal to 0, saying that they are non correlated at all

You would use add it when it makes sense to you, when would it be needed to have a covariance/correlation fixed to 0
